movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
With a wonderful resistance-laden defensive typing, as well as the ability to ignore most entry hazard damage, Corviknight is a premier defensive staple in the tier. Brave Bird hits Ogerpon-W, Rillaboom, and Iron Valiant hard while doing decent damage to Great Tusk and Enamorus. Brave Bird is generally best used on balance teams that struggle with Ogerpon-W and already contain solid answers to late-game Kingambit. Body Press hits Kingambit, Kyurem, and Ting-Lu especially well. It also has immediate synergy with Iron Defense, allowing Corviknight to more confidently handle physical setup sweepers such as Dragonite, Gliscor, and Kingambit, especially with Pressure to more quickly stall out their attacks' PP. Defog allows Corviknight to fulfill the role as the team's hazard remover, with Corviknight often finding ample opportunities to remove hazards against common setters such as Iron Treads, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor. Defog Corviknight can also beat them in the long term, as Pressure makes their hazard move's PP drain faster than Defog's. Defog is best used on teams with another form of hazard control, which allow Corviknight to act as the secondary hazard remover to alleviate the pressure on its teammate; this is especially valuable against non-Gholdengo teams. With U-turn, Corviknight becomes an exceptional pivot, using its excellent bulk and defensive typing to safely bring in teammates after taking a hit. The move is often best used on bulky offensive and balance teams that appreciate the momentum swing Corviknight adds, especially as an opportunity to bring terrifying wallbreakers onto the field. In addition to the provided combinations, a nicher set using Iron Defense, Body Press, Brave Bird, and Roost can be used on teams that want maximum proactivity from Corviknight, notably guaranteeing the matchup against even Tera Ghost Kingambit, though the lack of team support is noticeable. Corviknight generally prefers a physically defensive spread to better handle Dragonite, Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Kingambit, though 120 Speed EVs can also be run on IronPress variants to outspeed Adamant variants of Kingambit and Ursaluna. Alternatively, balance teams that struggle to handle Kyurem and Darkrai while having other checks for the aforementioned physical threats may appreciate a more specially defensive spread with 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpD and a Sassy nature. When running this variant, Corviknight should pick Brave Bird as its main attack, since the lower Defense investment will make Body Press much more ineffectual. Rocky Helmet is generally the preferred item to punish contact moves such as Landorus-T's and opposing Corviknight's U-turn and Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge, but Leftovers is also acceptable to help keep Corviknight slightly healthier, particularly helping to mitigate Stealth Rock damage, especially on specially defensive sets. Corviknight generally prefers Tera Dragon to resist Ogerpon-W's STAB attacks, as well as Fire-type attacks such as those from Cinderace and Heatran in a pinch. Tera Fighting can be used on Iron Defense + Body Press sets to make Corviknight a more reliable late-game Kingambit answer. Tera Water provides Fire and Water resistances similarly to Tera Dragon, but it also grants a better matchup against Weavile and Dragon Dance Kyurem. Many other defensive Tera types can be used for complementing specific team structures. For example, Tera Ice can be used on specially defensive sets to handle special Kyurem for bulkier balance teams with good hazard control, and Tera Ghost lets Corviknight beat Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta on teams without another sufficient answer to it.

Corviknight's flexibility in its moves and Tera type, as well as the role it fulfills, makes it a welcome choice on a myriad of team structures, ranging from stall to bulky offense. Stall teams will appreciate Corviknight for its ability to absorb Knock Off, remove hazards, switch into Great Tusk, and act as extra insurance against Kingambit. In return, Corviknight appreciates Blissey absorbing strong special attacks from threats such as Darkrai and Iron Moth, Galarian Weezing helping remove entry hazards against Gholdengo, and Dondozo checking physical setup threats such as Zamazenta. On balance and bulky offense teams, Galarian Slowking, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl are good teammates to help absorb strong special attacks from Zapdos, Raging Bolt, Iron Moth, and Heatran well; in return, Corviknight can switch into Great Tusk, Hisuian Samurott, Ogerpon-W, and Kingambit, which they fear. Corviknight and Galarian Slowking can also form a pivoting core together to bring in offensive teammates via U-turn and Chilly Reception, respectively, enhancing their synergy. Furthermore, Corviknight helps limit hazards with Defog and absorbs the debilitating Knock Off to enhance their longevity. Corviknight pairs well with wallbreakers such as Dragapult, Kyurem, and Ogerpon-W, as it can keep them healthy with hazard removal and find opportunities to bring them onto the field via U-turn, allowing them to continue to make progress for the team. Corviknight can additionally switch into common answers to these teammates such as Ting-Lu, Galarian Slowking, and Dragonite, respectively, further patching up the team's weaknesses. Cinderace is a great teammate on these squads to form a dual hazard removal core, with Cinderace threatening out and removing hazards against Gholdengo for Corviknight. Cinderace also can take a Fire-type attack such as Heatran's Magma Storm in a pinch and threaten slower wallbreakers like Ogerpon-W for Corviknight, while Corviknight can handle Landorus-T and Gliscor for Cinderace, especially as they're hazard setters that Cinderace is scared of.

movesets.name: Physically Defensive
movesets.description:
• Corviknight's high physical bulk gives it a strong defensive presence in the tier. It is one of the few consistent counters to strong Ground-types like Great Tusk, physical attackers like Chien-Pao, and some special attackers like non-Choice Specs Iron Bundle. Furthermore, its access to Defog also makes it a solid entry hazard remover, though it struggles against Gholdengo.
  • Body Press provides Corviknight with a way to leverage its high Defense stat, doing significant damage to Fighting-weak Pokemon.
  • Brave Bird allows Corviknight to threaten Flutter Mane and Great Tusk. Alternatively, Iron Head can be used to threaten the former while avoiding recoil damage.
  • Maximum HP investment and enough Defense to check Chien-Pao is combined with Leftovers and 96 Special Defense EVs, which allows Corviknight to take two Mystical Fires from most Flutter Mane, as well as giving it the ability to take on non-Choice Specs Iron Bundle and weaker attacks like Freeze-Dry from Choice Specs Iron Bundle.
  • Tera Steel or Flying can be used to shed the weaknesses of Corviknight's dual typing: Tera Steel allows Corviknight to resist Ice-type attacks from Chien-Pao, while Tera Flying allows Corviknight to resist Great Tusk's Fighting-type attacks. Depending on your choice, Terastallization also amplifies the power of either Iron Head or Brave Bird.
  • Corviknight works well as a part of a defensive core with Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Blissey, which can handle threats like Miraidon that obliterate Corviknight. Additionally, Corviknight makes a great partner for offensive threats like Chi-Yu, which appreciate a teammate that easily switches into Ting-Lu, or Great Tusk, which appreciates opposing Great Tusk being worn down.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive
movesets.description:
• Specially defensive Corviknight can switch into foes like Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, Gholdengo, and Glimmora.
  • U-turn is used to make Corviknight an effective defensive pivot that can maintain momentum against foes that force it out such as Miraidon and Koraidon.
  • Mirror Armor allows Corviknight to check Mystical Fire Flutter Mane, which would otherwise beat it. Alternatively, when paired with Pressure, Protect enables Corviknight to avoid being 2HKOed by Hydro Pump from Choice Specs Iron Bundle, as well as allowing Corviknight to deplete PP with Pressure more effectively.
  • Corviknight can use Tera Steel to get rid of its weakness to Electric and better take on Ice-type moves from Iron Bundle. Alternatively, it can opt to use Tera Ground to become immune to Miraidon's powerful Electro Drift.
  • Specially defensive Corviknight needs help dealing with strong physical wallbreakers such as Chien-Pao from teammates like Dondozo and Scream Tail. Furthermore, Pokemon that are especially threatened by Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle, such as Koraidon, Great Tusk, and Skeledirge, are able to rely on specially defensive Corviknight as a consistent switch-in.

movesets.name: Physically Defensive (Flying)
movesets.description:
Corviknight is a great physical wall for Flying teams, capable of handling the likes of Meowscarada and Iron Boulder while providing Defog support. Body Press makes use of Corviknight's respectable Defense to remove Steel- and Ice-types like Iron Treads, Bisharp, and Mamoswine. Iron Head handles foes not particularly bothered by Body Press such as Kleavor, Iron Boulder, and Enamorus. Alternatively, Brave Bird can OHKO threats like Lokix and Sneasler, OHKO Ogerpon-W after minor chip damage, and put immense pressure on Urshifu-R. 12 Attack EVs are used with Iron Head to allow Corviknight to OHKO Flutter Mane; otherwise, going for maximum Defense investment.

Gliscor and the Landorus formes' Electric immunity enables them to handle the likes of Raging Bolt and Iron Hands; they can also check Fire-types such as Iron Moth and Cinderace for Corviknight, along with setting Stealth Rock. Gliscor can further assist Corviknight by using Toxic to wear down opposing physical walls like Great Tusk and Sinistcha. Meanwhile, the Landorus formes equipped with a Choice Scarf can deal with Volcarona, Ogerpon-H, Gholdengo, and the aforementioned Iron Moth for Corviknight. Specially defensive Articuno can help tank Ice Beams from threats like Kyurem and Greninja and, thanks to Freeze-Dry and Haze, apply pressure to opposing Flying teams along with Water-types such as Pelipper and Primarina. Assault Vest Tornadus-T can assist against powerful special attackers like Iron Valiant and Hisuian Zoroark and provide Knock Off support to remove Rocky Helmet from foes like Ting-Lu and Skarmory. Choice Band Dragonite helps to handle Fire-types like Ceruledge and uses Extreme Speed to pick off fast foes like Meowscarada and Urshifu-R while appreciating Corviknight handling Ice- and Rock-types. Choice Scarf Enamorus can break through Dragon- and Dark-type threats like Choice Specs Dragapult, Kyurem, and Darkrai. Lastly, Nasty Plot Galarian Moltres can check the likes of Gholdengo and Pecharunt that Corviknight struggles to touch while enjoying Corviknight using Iron Head to remove Fairy-types like Enamorus. Gyarados can help to handle physical attackers like Mamoswine and Ceruledge thanks to Intimidate along with threats like Volcarona.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive (Flying)
movesets.description:
Specially defensive Corviknight serves an important role on Flying by being able to sponge special attacks from the likes of Frosmoth, Greninja, and Flutter Mane. Iron Head threatens the Fairy- and Ice-types that can scare Flying, like Hatterene, Iron Valiant, and Kyurem. U-turn allows for Corviknight to safely pivot in teammates. Defog eases entry for teammates like Choice Band Dragonite. The given EV spread maximizes Corviknight's special bulk while allowing it to OHKO Flutter Mane with Iron Head.

The Landorus formes can check problematic Electric-, Fire-, and Steel-types like Raging Bolt, Hisuian Arcanine, and Gholdengo for Corviknight while appreciating it being able to take on special Ice-type attacks from the likes of Articuno and Darkrai. Choice Scarf variants of the Landorus formes can also outspeed and remove Flutter Mane and Hoopa-U. Gliscor threatens Electric- and Steel-types like Sandy Shocks and Heatran while also providing Toxic support to wear down bulky targets like Swampert and Pelipper. Skarmory serves as a solid defensive partner for Corviknight, being able to comfortably take on physical Rock- and Ice-types like Kleavor and Cetitan, as well as other physical threats like Meowscarada, along with providing entry hazard support. Dragonite greatly appreciates Corviknight handling Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Hatterene. In return, Dragonite can easily remove Fire-types such as Iron Moth and Ninetales and pick off threats like Meowscarada with Extreme Speed. Assault Vest Tornadus-T assists Corviknight by using Knock Off to remove Choice Specs from the likes of Flutter Mane, giving Corviknight an easier time handling them. Additionally, Tornadus-T can use its Flying-type attack to remove Iron Valiant and Ogerpon-W. Zapdos can handle Water-types that resist Corviknight's Iron Head like Toxapex, Empoleon, and Swords Dance Urshifu-R along with checking opposing Corviknight. Choice Scarf Enamorus deals with Dragon- and Dark-types like Choice Specs Dragapult, Choice Specs Greninja, and Hisuian Samurott along with providing Healing Wish for Corviknight if necessary. Gyarados can help to stave off physical threats like Cinderace, Barraskewda, and Gallade along with spreading paralysis, enabling Corviknight to outspeed Glimmora, which makes it easier to check.

movesets.name: Bulk Up (Steel)
movesets.description:
Bulk Up Corviknight serves as a solid wincon for Steel teams thanks to its solid natural bulk and Flying typing, granting it a key immunity and neutrality to Ground and Fighting, respectively. Brave Bird is Corviknight's main offensive tool, easily removing Fighting-types like Gallade, Sneasler, and Scrafty along with dealing with other problematic foes like Dragapult and Ogerpon-W. Body Press provides a solid complement to Brave Bird, helping to deal with the Steel- and Rock-types that resist Brave Bird such as Bisharp, Empoleon, and Ogerpon-C. Alternatively, Taunt can be used to stop attempts to handle Corviknight with opposing threats such as Whirlwind Hippowdon and Haze Toxapex; otherwise, Substitute enables Corviknight to easily set up in front of the likes of Dragon Tail Garchomp, punishes defensive pivots such as Mandibuzz and opposing Corviknight, and grants it a safety net against wallbreakers that would otherwise threaten it out. The main EV spread maximizes Corviknight's special bulk, while the alternative EV spread can be used to let Corviknight outspeed Skarmory and use Taunt against it before it can set up Iron Defense or Roost, enabling Corviknight to eventually win.

Heatran serves as an excellent teammate, easily taking on the Fire-types that would handle Corviknight such as Iron Moth, Skeledirge, and opposing Heatran along with absorbing Will-O-Wisp from the likes of Dragapult and Moltres. Iron Treads's Ground typing allows it to easily handle the Electric-types that threaten Corviknight like Raging Bolt and Sandy Shocks; it also removes Landorus with Ice Spinner, preventing it from grounding Corviknight with Gravity. Gholdengo can help Corviknight by using Thunder Wave to slow down threats like Ogerpon-W as well as handling foes such as Iron Valiant and Pecharunt. Archaludon can handle physical attackers that threaten to break Corviknight like Ogerpon-H and Urshifu-R thanks to Stamina. Alternatively, Choice Scarf Archaludon can outspeed and remove threats such as Keldeo with Thunderbolt. Hisuian Goodra is a nice special wall capable of taking on threats like Flutter Mane, Latios, and Dragapult along with being able to use Knock Off to remove Rocky Helmet from the likes of Toxapex and Skarmory. Bisharp can remove problematic Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Sableye as well as use Sucker Punch to check fast threats like Hoopa-U.

movesets.name: Defog (Steel)
movesets.description: This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

movesets.name: Defog (Flying)
movesets.description:
Corviknight is an invaluable part of Flying teams by virtue of its incredible defensive typing and access to utility options that many of its teammates appreciate. Defog removes Stealth Rock so that its teammates that don't run Heavy-Duty Boots or had theirs removed have an easier time switching in. Defog also removes dual screens set by foes, allowing its wallbreaking teammates to remove various threats. Iron Head threatens Rock- and Ice-types that can threaten its teammates such as Iron Boulder, Ogerpon-C, and Alolan Ninetales. Body Press handles Rock- and Ice-types as well, and in addition, it handles Steel- and Dark-types such as Excadrill, Bisharp, and Greninja. Alternatively, U-turn allows Corviknight to pivot out of bad matchups such as Fire- and Electric-types. Pressure allows it to punish Sableye using Encore. On the other hand, Mirror Armor can be used to punish attacks such as Bleakwind Storm from Tornadus-T and Moonblast from the likes of Iron Valiant and Enamorus. A Careful nature along with 252 HP EVs and 144 Special Defense EVs allow Corviknight to survive two Shadow Balls from Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and 12 Attack EVs let it OHKO back with Iron Head.

Landorus appreciates Corviknight removing Stealth Rock, which would otherwise wear it down over time due to its lack of recovery. In return, Landorus takes out Fire-types such as Heatran, Ceruledge, and Hisuian Arcanine, and its Electric immunity eases that matchup, handling the likes of Raging Bolt and Magnezone. Skarmory is another beneficiary of Corviknight's removal of entry hazards, as it preserves Sturdy so it is able to set its own entry hazards. Articuno, with its great special bulk, takes on Water-types such as Choice Specs Greninja and Primarina and threatens them back with Freeze-Dry. In return, it appreciates Corviknight handling Rock-types. Choice Specs Zapdos and Choice Band Dragonite are two more offensive teammates that appreciate the removal of entry hazards, which would otherwise weaken them. Zapdos also appreciates Corviknight taking out Rock-types such as Ogerpon-C and Kleavor, while Dragonite appreciates the removal of Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Hatterene. In return, Zapdos handles Primarina, while Dragonite takes on Fire-types such as Ogerpon-H and Heatran. Choice Scarf Enamorus provides great speed control for Flying teams, outspeeding and threatening the likes of Dragapult and Choice Specs Iron Valiant. In return, Enamorus appreciates Corviknight taking on Steel- and Ice-types such as Excadrill, Empoleon, and Weavile. Setup sweepers such as Double Dance Galarian Moltres and Dragon Dance Dragonite appreciate Corviknight walling and removing their threats so they can find opportunities to set up and sweep late-game.

movesets.name: Pivot Knight
movesets.description:
• Corviknight's fantastic typing makes it a great physically defensive pivot, easily getting dangerous teammates in such as Chien-Pao, Flutter Mane, and Ogerpon-H in.

  • Body Press versus Iron Head: Body Press has decent damage output and helps massively against common Dark-types like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S. Meanwhile, Iron Head ensures that Corviknight will not be walled by Flutter Mane.

  • Taunt: Corviknight might not be fast, but it's fast enough to shut down most other defensive Pokemon with Taunt, such as Ting-Lu and Toxapex.

  • Brave Bird: Brave Bird's recoil is unwelcome, but it's a fantastic response against Ogerpon-H, who otherwise will scare Corviknight off.

  • Neutral Speed Natures versus Negative Speed Natures with a Speed IV of 4 or 5: Negative Speed natures are handy for giving very slow U-turns when used in conjunction with lower Speed IVs, as well as not risking getting hit by Ursaluna-B's Earth Power while using Roost. Just note that going any lower than 4 Speed IVs will underspeed Ting-Lu before it can be shut down by Taunt, and powerful Special attackers like Primarina outspeeding Corviknight can be a problem for some teams.

Other Options
  • Tailwind: Tailwind is an incredible support move for making powerful sweepers like Urshifu-R even more difficult to revenge kill, though its short time span can make it tricky to fully take advantage of.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Corviknight's defensive typing is fantastic, so don't Terastallize too hastily, or else it'll lose to threats it normally checks.

  • Dragon: Dragon and Fairy weaknesses are devastating, but in the late-game, resisting Electric and Fire can give Corviknight new win conditions against foes such as Ogerpon-H that lack Play Rough and Tera Water Urshifu-R. Just note that Modest Tera Fire Choice Specs Chi-Yu can still OHKO with Overheat.

  • Fire: Tera Fire may not seem like a good fit for a pivot due to the Stealth Rock weakness, but it vastly improves Corviknight's chances of defeating Ogerpon-H and Tera Electric Chien-Pao, making it a worthy defensive choice. Do note that this won't help much against Choice Specs Chi-Yu.

  • Flying: While this set doesn't always use Brave Bird, Tera Flying lets Corviknight keep its typing while using Roost, meaning Earthquake and Fissure can no longer hit Corviknight while its restoring health. It also improves Corviknight's chances against Ogerpon-H.

  • Water: With Tera Water, Corviknight consistently survives all but Modest Tera Fire Choice Specs Chi-Yu's Overheat, letting it deal serious damage with Body Press. It also gains a key resistance to Ice for Chien-Pao and Water for Tera Water Urshifu-R.

  • Fighting: Getting STAB on Body Press can give Corviknight a surprisingly decent chance at cleaning weakened teams, though this makes it especially vulnerable to Flutter Mane.

  • Electric: While turning Corviknight's incredible Ground-type immunity into a weakness is unfortunate, Tera Electric otherwise improves a wide variety of match-ups, with Tera Electric Chien-Pao and Raging Bolt being particularly major ones.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: This lets Corviknight wear down physical threats more quickly while pivoting.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers's consistent recovery can be quite helpful for taking repeated hits from Ruination when attempting to stall it out with Pressure.

Abilities

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor's ability to punish Flutter Mane for using Mystical Fire makes it a great ability choice on Corviknight.

  • Pressure: Corviknight's excellent bulk and Taunt makes Pressure a good alternative for stalling out foes such as Gliscor and Ting-Lu.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 76 Def / 180 SpD with Impish or Relaxed This spread has enough bulk to avoid a 2HKO from Timid Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump as long as they lack an offensive item, which can be especially useful if using Pressure. Just beware of Iron Bundle's Encore.

  • 252 HP / 20 Def / 236 SpD with Careful or Sassy: This specially defensive spread won't check major physical threats like Dragonite nearly as well, but it does avoid a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

movesets.name: IronPress
movesets.description:
• Corviknight stands out as one of the best choices around for sweeping with Iron Defense and Body Press, thanks to its excellent typing and Roost.

  • Iron Head versus Brave Bird: Iron Head ensures Flutter Mane isn't a reliable check to Corviknight, in addition to making it an even better Swords Dance Mimikyu check. Brave Bird is less reliable at beating Flutter Mane, but severely punishes Ogerpon-H switch-ins.

  • U-turn versus Taunt: While U-turn with this set may seem strange, Corviknight is still a decent pivot even if it must give up Taunt. Just note that this keaves Corviknight completely walled by Ghost-types like Flutter Mane. Taunt on the other hand, lets Corviknight effectively shut down slower defensive Pokemon, such as Ting-Lu and Dondozo. Note that both options leave Corviknight hopelessly walled by Flutter Mane.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Corviknight has a fantastic defensive typing, so only Terastallize if you need to win certain matchups, especially since it becomes vulnerable to Toxic.

  • Fighting: With a Fighting Tera type, Body Press is easier to sweep with, with many Ting-Lu variants now being 2HKOed by boosted Body Press. It also gets rid of enough of Corviknight's common weaknesses that foes like Ogerpon-H and Raging Bolt will check Corviknight far less reliably.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Corviknight a way to resist both Chien-Pao's and Chi-Yu's most powerful STAB attacks, though Modest Tera Fire Choice Specs Chi-Yu can still OHKO with Overheat. It also stops Tera Water Urshifu-R from cleaving through Corviknight's Iron Defense with Surging Strikes.

  • Dragon: A Dragon Tera type lets Corviknight resist common attacks aimed at it, such as Electric- and Fire-type attacks from foes like Raging Bolt and Ogerpon-H respectively. However, the new weaknesses to Fairy and Dragon make this an especially reactive Terastallization.

  • Fire: While Tera Fire leaves Corviknight extremely vulnerable to Urshifu-R, in exchange it retains the important Fairy-type resistance and does well against Ogerpon-H.

  • Flying: A Flying Tera type lets Corviknight retain its Flying typing even when using Roost, making it a more reliable check to Fissure users such as Dondozo and Garganacl.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: The passive damage from Rocky Helmet against foes like Dragonite give Corviknight a much easier time using U-turn over Iron Head.

  • Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Since this Corviknight attempts to sweep, Sitrus Berry's burst of quick recovery can make it less pressured to spend a turn using Roost. Leftovers on the other hand, will still keep healing Corviknight even after being hit by Ruination, so it can make sense with Pressure.

  • Maranga Berry: A Special Defense boost granted from Maranga Berry makes it far more difficult for foes like Flutter Mane to revenge kill Corviknight, and it can even be paired with Terastallization to defeat Raging Bolt!

  • Covert Cloak: When paired with Taunt, Covert Cloak makes Corviknight an effective Garganacl check provided that it isn't Tera Ghost, though note Corviknight will no longer drop Flutter Mane's Special Attack with Mirror Armor.

Abilities

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor means Flutter Mane can't use Mystical Fire without getting its Special Attack dropped, unless Corviknight is holding Covert Cloak.

  • Pressure: Corviknight's ability to take powerful, low PP moves such as Close Combat after Iron Defense makes Pressure a viable alternative, in addition to giving Corviknight a better chance of dealing with Ruination from Ting-Lu effectively.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 76 Def / 180 SpD with Impish The Special Defense investment stops Iron Bundle from 2HKOing Corviknight with Hydro Pump, especially useful if revenge killing one with Body Press. Just remember that Encore means Corviknight is still vulnerable to Iron Bundle ruining set up attempts.

  • 252 HP / 20 Def / 236 SpD with Careful: While Body Press will be significantly weaker on this specially defensive spread, it does avoid a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball, making this spread especially effective with Iron Head and Mirror Armor.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
• With Bulk Up giving an Attack boost, Corviknight is free from having to use Body Press for good damage output, making it easier to run Taunt against defensive foes without fear of being walled by Ghost-types like Flutter Mane.

  • Iron Head versus Brave Bird: Iron Head reliably 2HKOs Chien-Pao without a boost and is a fantastic tool against Flutter Mane, while Brave Bird is a great response against Ogerpon-H and the only hope of 2HKOing Chi-Yu.

  • Physically Defensive versus Specially Defensive: Physically Defensive Corviknight takes on common Pokemon like Dragon Dance Dragonite and Urshifu-R more comfortably, while focusing on Special Defense stops Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane from 2HKOing Corviknight with Shadow Ball.

Other Options
  • Power Trip: Power Trip takes several boosts to get powerful, but it's Corviknight's best shot at dealing decent damage to Gholdengo. It also makes Corviknight a viable option on Baton Pass Blaziken teams, especially since it relies less on Terastallization to defeat Dark-types than Latias.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Remember that most of Corviknight's good Tera types leave it vulnerable to Toxic, so Terastallize carefully and only win a win condition is clear.

  • Water: Tera Water is an effective tool against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, though note that Choice Specs Chi-Yu can OHKO with Tera Fire boosted Overheat. It also prevents Urshifu-R from revenge killing Corviknight with Tera-boosted Surging Strikes.

  • Flying: This Tera type lets Corviknight retain its Flying typing while using Roost, meaning Fissure users such as Dondozo are much easier to handle, and giving Brave Bird a healthy boost in power.

  • Dragon: Once Fairy-, Ice-, and Dragon-types are out of the way, the Dragon Tera type allows Corviknight to turn the tables on most Ogerpon-H.

  • Fire: There are few better Tera-types to use against Ogerpon-H than Tera Fire, which unlike Tera Dragon, will retain an important Fairy resistance. It does make Urshifu-R a huge problem as a drawback.

  • Dark: If using Power Trip, Tera Dark is highly recommended to boost its damage output.

Abilities

  • Mirror Armor: In addition to punishing Flutter Mane for using Mystical Fire when not using Covert Cloak, Mirror Armor stops pivoting Intimidate foes like Landorus-T and Incineroar from softening Corviknight's damage output.

  • Pressure: Pressure is a reasonable alternative for whittling down PP, which can be especially helpful against Ting-Lu's troublesome Ruination.

Items

  • Covert Cloak: When paired with Taunt, Corviknight can effectively take down Garganacl.

  • Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Sitrus Berry is preferred due to the quicker burst of recovery better fitting a sweeper, but Leftovers can work very well with Pressure in an attempt to out-stall Ruination.

  • Maranga Berry: Maranga Berry's Special Defense boost can stop Special Attacking foes like Flutter Mane from 2HKOing physically defensive Corviknight.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Physically Defensive Corviknight sets can use Well-Baked Body to check a wide variety of Fire-types, including Cinderace, Ogerpon-H, Moltres, Heatran, and Iron Moth lacking Discharge; however, it loses a lot of bulk and results in worse matchups against Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and offensive Great Tusk. Specially defensive sets can use Water Absorb to check Ogerpon-W, Manaphy, and Choice Specs Primarina while preventing Swampert and Primarina from pivoting out with Flip Turn or Bulletproof to let Corviknight check Cinderace, Moltres, Choice Specs Primarina, and Gholdengo lacking Thunderbolt, but Corviknight often gets getter value out of its other abilities. Corviknight can run a set with Bulk Up, Agility, Roost, and Power Trip with an immunity ability such as Volt Absorb on hyper offense teams to surprise opponents and potentially sweep teams if lacking appropriate checks.

Checks and Counters

Electric-type Moves: Without Volt Absorb, Corviknight gets destroyed by Electric-types like Zapdos and Sandy Shocks as well as Electric-type move coverage like Thunderbolt Latios and Deoxys-S.

Fire-types: Without Well-Baked Body, Fire-types like Iron Moth, Moltres, Cinderace, and Heatran easily defeat Corviknight.

Strong Special Attackers: Choice Specs Gholdengo and Primarina can 2HKO Corviknight even if it's running maximum HP and Special Defense EVs.

movesets.name: Physically Defensive
movesets.description:
Corviknight's great defensive typing and solid utility moves make it a defensive staple in the tier, checking physical threats like Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and Great Tusk. Fluffy is the generally preferred ability, as it provides Corviknight with more physical bulk, letting it have a much easier time checking the aforementioned physical attackers, along with Kingambit. Intimidate gives Corviknight a better matchup into Chien-Pao, Mold Breaker Great Tusk, and the Ogerpon formes excluding Ogerpon-H. Corviknight favors Brave Bird due to its higher power and ability to deal significant damage to Great Tusk and Zamazenta, but Body Press can be used to hit Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, and Kingambit. U-turn helps Corviknight's allies by generating momentum, Roost gives it longevity, and Defog removes entry hazards to aid Stealth Rock-weak partners like Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-H. Rocky Helmet punishes Great Tusk and non-Magic Guard Roaring Moon and Zamazenta as well as the many U-turn pivots like Corviknight in the tier, while Leftovers provides Corviknight with extra longevity. Corviknight runs 0 Speed IVs and a Relaxed nature to grants its allies safe entry with U-turn.

Corviknight is used mostly on offense and balance structures that appreciate its defensive prowess, entry hazard removal, and ability to provide slow pivoting. RegenVest Pokemon like Swampert, Manaphy, and Primarina are heavily reliant on their Assault Vest, so Corviknight aids them by functioning as a Knock Off absorber from users like Roaring Moon, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads. Special attackers like Gholdengo, Zapdos, and Iron Moth are quite threatening to Corviknight, so specially defensive checks like Manaphy, Swampert, and Roaring Moon are much appreciated. Fire-types like Cinderace and Ogerpon-H scare Corviknight; therefore, it requires checks to them like Pecharunt, Moltres, and Primordial Sea Zapdos. If using Fluffy, Corviknight struggles against Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-W, so checks to them like Manaphy and Moltres, respectively, are quite helpful. If using Intimidate, Corviknight benefits from Pecharunt and Scream Tail to take on strong physical attackers like Choice Band Zamazenta.

movesets.name: Dual Screens
movesets.description:
With its remarkable defensive profile and utility options, Prankster Corviknight becomes an effective lead at setting dual screens to support its teammates. Prankster-boosted Taunt allows Corviknight to shut down foes like Great Tusk, Skarmory, and Regieleki from setting their entry hazards or own dual screens; stop Cinderace and opposing Corviknight from removing its dual screens with Court Change and Defog; prevent offensive threats like Zamazenta, all Ogerpon formes, and Iron Boulder from using it as setup fodder; block Trick from Choice item users like Scream Tail and Gholdengo from crippling it; and additionally stop defensive Pokemon like Gholdengo, Scream Tail, and non-Prankster Pecharunt from healing freely, letting its teammates overwhelm them more easily. U-turn makes use of Corviknight's middling Speed tier to support its teammates by bringing them in safely after stomaching an attack, and it's especially valuable against Dark-type foes like Chien-Pao, Kingambit, and Taunt Roaring Moon that can otherwise set up in front of or even shut down Corviknight.

Corviknight is exclusively found on dual screens hyper offense teams. As a result, high caliber offensive threats like Tail Glow Manaphy, IronPress Zamazenta, and Dragon Dance Roaring Moon pair well with it, as they appreciate Corviknight bringing them in safely through U-turn and its dual screens to set up more easily. However, Double Dance sweepers such as Iron Crown and Galarian Moltres benefit from said dual screens even more, as they require multiple turns of setup before wreaking havoc. Other setup sweepers like Iron Boulder, Iron Hands, and Kingambit have the added benefit of threatening Cinderace and Defoggers like opposing Corviknight and Mandibuzz—especially since Mandibuzz can use Defog freely even in the face of Corviknight—preventing them any free opportunities of ever removing Corviknight's dual screens. Since other foes like Zapdos, Iron Moth, and Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Kingambit can also use Corviknight as entry points, teammates that can come in afterwards to either threaten or use them as setup fodder are also beneficial, with the aforementioned Iron Boulder, Deoxys-S, Zamazenta, and Great Tusk capable of doing so. Furthermore, Corviknight's ability to prevent Stealth Rock from going up with Taunt also gives setup sweepers like Ogerpon-Hearthflame and Chien-Pao more opportunities to get rolling.

movesets.name: Immunity
movesets.description:
Corviknight's great utility and defensive typing, further bolstered by an immunity-granting ability, make it an excellent special wall and defensive pivot. Volt Absorb lets it counter Electric-types such as Zapdos and Sandy Shocks and helps against special attackers that rely on Electric-type coverage, such as Deoxys-S, Latios, and Iron Crown. Similarly, Well-Baked Body shuts down Ogerpon-H, Moltres, and non-Discharge Iron Moth. Brave Bird is the go-to STAB move, while Body Press is an option on Well-Baked Body sets to take advantage of the Defense boosts. U-turn generates momentum for Corviknight’s teammates, and Defog provides valuable hazard control. A Sassy nature with 0 Speed IVs is crucial for Corviknight's role as a slow pivot.

Corviknight fits on balance and bulky offense teams, where its longevity and consistency gives it a niche over Iron Treads. Corviknight can pivot in more offensive teammates like Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-H, which also appreciate its ability to remove entry hazards. Corviknight is threatened by physical wallbreakers such as Zamazenta and Ogerpon-W, making physically defensive walls like Great Tusk and Pecharunt good teammates. Corviknight can also be overwhelmed by neutral special attacks from Gholdengo and Primarina, so it needs backup from RegenVest users like Manaphy and Swampert. In exchange, Volt Absorb Corviknight helps Manaphy answer Electric-types, while Well-Baked Body helps Swampert answer Fire-types carrying Grass-type coverage like Iron Moth and Heatran.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 4 Onwards

Price Range: 12-13 points

Overview: Corviknight is a solid utility Pokemon due to its fantastic defensive typing, highly customizable bulk, and decent utility movepool. While it is excellent at supporting a team's offensive capabilities through U-turn and Defog, Corviknight struggles to deal damage due to its poor offensive stats and is liable to being setup fodder due to its lack of Toxic or phazing moves. Despite facing stiff competition as a pivot, Corviknight still has a decent niche in enabling offensively drafted teams by being a slow pivot and providing secondary hazard removal.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Defensive Pivot: Corviknight's primary role is to pivot into opposing attackers and safely bring in your own. This set is generally run with heavy defensive investment, tailored to your opponent's draft, and minimum Speed. The combination of Roost, U-turn, and Defog allows it to pivot in and potentially remove hazards multiple times per game. Brave Bird is usually the best attacking move for Corviknight, but Drill Peck, Iron Head, Body Press, or some combination of the aforementioned moves are alternatives depending on the matchup.

Setup Sweeper: Corviknight is capable of using its high natural bulk to set up on slower threats or weak attackers with Bulk Up or Iron Defense. Once opposing Fire- and Electric-type attackers are significantly weakened or removed, Corviknight can become nearly impossible to deal with once it is set up and can close out games.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Brave Bird, Iron Head, Drill Peck

Setup Moves: Bulk Up, Iron Defense

Utility Moves: Roost, Defog, U-turn, Taunt

Coverage: Body Press

Niche Moves

Light Screen / Reflect: Corviknight has access to dual screens, allowing it to forgo its usual utility in favor of supporting teammates with dual screens and safe entry with U-turn.

Agility and Power Trip: A combination of Agility, Bulk Up, and Power Trip can turn Corviknight into a fearsome sweeper in the right matchup. This set may also utilize Weakness Policy to forgo the necessary turns spent using Bulk Up to strengthen Power Trip.

Tailwind: Corviknight can provide speed control to its teammates with Tailwind + U-turn.

Common Items

Leftovers: Leftovers supplements Corviknight's reliable recovery with Roost and is more effective in keeping it healthy with reliable hazard removal or on setup sets.

Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet is usually Corviknight's only option to chip opposing Pokemon using U-turn or Flip Turn. Rocky Helmet can also help Corviknight win some one-on-one matchups where physical contact is expected, such as versus Palafin and Great Tusk.

Heavy-Duty Boots: While Corviknight enjoys an immunity to Spikes and Toxic Spikes, its Stealth Rock neutrality limits its ability to pivot and Defog; Heavy-Duty Boots removes this limitation and has more free turns to use Roost and Defog.

Niche Items

Eject Button: As Corviknight can often find itself switching into a U-turn only to be faced with an incoming powerful Fire- or Electric-type, Eject Button allows Corviknight to safely pivot out and steal the momentum back once in a battle.

Weakness Policy: Corviknight can utilize its mixed bulk to tank a super effective attack such as Volt Switch or a weak Flamethrower and use Agility, turning it into a deadly sweeper.

Light Clay: Only used with dual screens, Light Clay allows Corviknight's screens to stick on the field longer for its teammates.

Red Card: Red Card is another option to stop opposing setup sweepers from taking advantage of Corviknight.

Tera

Corviknight should rarely be considered as a Tera Captain due to its already excellent defensive typing. Carefully consider the matchup if you must use Corviknight as a Tera user, as Terastallization will either get rid of its immunity to grounded entry hazards or gain a new weakness to Stealth Rock. Corviknight should only consider Tera on offensive sets, giving a new defensive typing that grants it more time to set up for a sweep. Tera Dark is one option, as it boosts the damage dealt by Power Trip, while Tera Flying is another option that can increase damage dealt by Brave Bird.

Draft Strategy

Corviknight is best drafted on offensively-oriented teams after you have first secured several premier attacking threats. Due to its strengths in typing, bulk, and non-requirement for Tera, it is extremely versatile with the types of attacking threats you choose to surround it with, as it rarely overlaps roles with most offensive Pokemon. Since it has little way to combat setup and is unable to spread Toxic, it typically performs poorly on more balanced and defensively-oriented teams, so keep this in mind when drafting Corviknight.

Offensive Partners: Corviknight tends to draw out opposing Fire- and Electric-type Pokemon, making Ground-type Pokemon good partners for Corviknight to pivot in. Pokemon like Garchomp and Great Tusk are excellent partners, as they are able to immediately threaten out opposing Fire- and Electric-types and attack or set up hazards. Thanks to Corviknight's low Speed, it is also able to offer support to frail and powerful wallbreakers like Chi-Yu, Iron Valiant, and Enamorus.

Defensive Partners: As Corviknight is vulnerable to being set up on and cannot punish with phazing or Toxic, it often appreciates partners that can fill these roles. Defensively, Unaware users such as Clodsire, Dondozo, and Skeledirge make decent partners to halt opposing setup sweepers. Corviknight also appreciates partners that can cover one or more of its weaknesses and use phazing moves, such as Iron Hands or and Hippowdon.

Entry Hazard Control: Corviknight is one of the most reliable Defoggers, but it rarely can function as a team's primary form of hazard control due to its relatively passive nature and often gets in the way of maintaining your own hazards. Defogging also often results in a huge loss of momentum, which is generally unadvisable for offensive teams. Corviknight enjoys having a teammate with Rapid Spin such as Great Tusk or Donphan to remove Stealth Rock, enabling items other than Heavy-Duty Boots.

Checks and Counters

Setup Sweepers: Corviknight's low Speed and lack of Toxic and Whirlwind open it up to being taken advantage of by faster setup sweepers, where Corviknight can only attempt to punish them with a slower Taunt or pivot to a teammate to handle the threat.

Fire-type Attackers: Corviknight can often do little in the face of opposing Fire-types, taking massive damage and risking a burn from most Fire-type attacks, further reducing its poor offensive output. It is often fodder for Pokemon such as Gouging Fire and Chi-Yu, which can proceed to set up with Dragon Dance or launch powerful attacks and threaten to OHKO Corviknight.

Electric-type Attackers: Electric-types resist both of Corviknights STAB types and can punish Corviknight with their powerful STAB moves or generate momentum through Volt Switch. Pokemon like Zapdos and Rotom-W threaten to OHKO or severely damage Corviknight, and Pokemon like Raging Bolt can easily set up Calm Mind in front of its face.

Taunt: Faster Pokemon are able to deny Corviknight's support moves with Taunt, stopping it from Defogging, using Roost, or setting up.

movesets.name: Bulky Setup
movesets.description: Corviknight is a potent setup user thanks to its fantastic bulk, useful defensive utility and typing, and ability to punish opposing physical setup from the likes of Dragonite and Great Tusk. IronPress allows for more instant anti-setup pressure, notably switching into and beating Fire Punch Dragonite without issue, while physically defensive Bulk Up + Brave Bird is better at dealing more instantaneous damage, especially Flying-weak or Fighting-resistant Pokemon like Urshifu-RS and Spectrier. U-turn in combination with Sablenite allows Corviknight to keep its ability to bounce entry hazards without hassle while bringing in frailer teammates like Urshifu-RS and Dragapult, while Defog is a better option on fatter teams where momentum isn't as necessary. Specially defensive variants can use both a Relaxed and Sassy nature depending on the team's needs, while physically defensive variants should always use a Relaxed nature. Venusaurite is useful on physically defensive Bulk Up + Brave Bird variants to answer the likes of Hisuian Arcanine and Iron Moth in a pinch while denying Stealth Rock from the former in conjunction with Defog. Corviknight fits best on balance and stall teams, with some viability on bulky offense teams thanks to its defensive prowess. Teammates like Urshifu-R and Raging Bolt adore Corviknight's ability to slow pivot them onto the field while blocking most entry hazard-setting attempts from the likes of Magearna, faster Garganacl variants, and the Arceus formes. Corviknight fears Garganacl's Salt Cure, notably chunking it every turn for 1/4 of its health, so answers like Lopunnite Iron Boulder, Great Tusk, and Urshifu-RS are greatly appreciated; Substitute Arceus-Ghost can also use non-Pinsirite Garganacl as setup fodder. Stronger Fire-types like Heatran, along with Iron Moth and Hisuian Arcanine when excluding Venusaurite, greatly pressure Corviknight, so answers like Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, Arceus-Water, and Ho-Oh are necessary. Electric-types like Regieleki and Raging Bolt are also extremely problematic for Corviknight, so answers like non-Fighting-type Great Tusk, Arceus-Ground, Eternatus, and Altarianite Dragonite are essential. Venusaurite variants should be paired with an alternative Sablenite user like Blissey, Hippowdon, or Cresselia, as entry hazard denial is especially important on bulkier teams.

movesets.name: Maranga Berry
movesets.description:
• Iron Defense lets Corviknight boost its Defense against physical attackers like non-Thunder Punch Meowscarada, non-Trick Choice Scarf Metagross, and Haxorus to then outheal them with Roost.
  • Taunt lets Corviknight beat setup Pokemon like Iron Crown, Calm Mind Primarina, and Registeel.
  • Running Agility on Corviknight over Body Press can allow it beat Curse Pecharunt, Encore + Disable Alolan Ninetales, and some Icy Wind variants of Primarina.
  • Compared to Agility, Body Press has much less chances of getting hit by a critical hit, allows Corviknight to beat Chien-Pao while reducing the chances of getting flinched, and is less forced to use Roost more than it has to against Ursaluna and Ursaluna-B thanks to not worrying about Roost letting it get hit by a Ground-type move or critical hit.
  • Maranga Berry allows Corviknight to beat special attackers such as Kyurem, Primarina, and Espathra.
  • Corviknight can reduce its chances of receiving a critical hit with Pressure, which is valuable on a stall Pokemon because its effect gives foes half as many chances to land a critical hit.
  • The 200 speed EVs allow Corviknight to outspeed neutral-natured base 60 Speed Pokemon such as Choice Specs Primarina and Sylveon and prevent them from setting up with Taunt, and the rest of the EVs are put into its defenses.
  • Good partners to Corviknight are Ground- and Dragon-types like Ursaluna and Roaring Moon that can beat the Fire- and Electric-types that threaten Corviknight super effectively.

movesets.name: Pressure Stall
movesets.description:
• Corviknight aims to use Pressure to deplete the PP of slower Pokemon without Speed-boosting moves, forcing them to damage themselves with Struggle.
  • The combination of Protect and Substitute allows Corviknight to stall most moves powerful enough to OHKO or 2HKO it, such as those used by Iron Hands and Donphan.
  • Taunt will prevent Pokemon such as non-Life Orb Primarina, Pecharunt, and Cresselia from using setup or status moves to overpower Corviknight.
  • The HP EVs allow for the maximum number of Substitutes, factoring in Leftovers and Protect, while maximum Speed EVs allow Corviknight to outrun Primarina as well as non-Timid Raging Bolt and Volcanion.
  • In order to mitigate Corviknight's weakness to Fire- and Electric-type moves from foes such as Volcanion, Raging Bolt, and Volcarona, it can be advantageous to pair it with Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra, Haxorus, and Dragapult.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description: The first EV spread allows Corviknight to survive two Mega Lopunny Close Combat after Stealth Rock.

movesets.name: Defensive Pivot (Flying)
movesets.description: With crucial neutralities to Rock and Ice, as well as several other resistances that let it wall several metagame threats such as Mamoswine, Mega Lopunny, and Iron Boulder, Corviknight is a solid entry hazard remover and pivot that mitigates the weakness to Stealth Rock commonly found on Flying teams. Body Press minimizes its passivity, notably hitting foes such as Mega Lopunny, Weavile, and Ogerpon-C, but Iron Head can be used instead to hit Fairy-types like Iron Valiant, Mega Diancie, and Alolan Ninetales. Pressure ensures that Corviknight doesn't run out of Defog PP as easily because it can switch into foes setting up Stealth Rock and lower their PP, such as Piloswine, Archaludon, and Ferrothorn, but Mirror Armor can be used instead to avoid a 2HKO from Mega Diancie's Mystical Fire. The first EV spread, even if Corviknight loses Leftovers, avoids a 2HKO from Mega Gallade's Close Combat, a 2HKO from Mega Lopunny's Close Combat after Stealth Rock, and an OHKO from Great Tusk's +1 All-Out Pummeling. However, the alternate EV spread still avoids a 2HKO from Mega Lopunny's Close Combat, and it avoids a 2HKO from Choice Specs Protean Greninja's Ice Beam with Leftovers recovery. Mantine is a solid partner for Corviknight, as it can switch into Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, and Heatran, and it also forms a defensive core by more consistently handling special attackers for it. Corviknight's role compression also allows Mantine to run Toxic over Defog, or if Mantine is desired as a Defogger instead, Corviknight can run Iron Head + Body Press. Gliscor and Landorus are also good allies to switch into Electric-types that force out Corviknight such as Zapdos, Raging Bolt, Zeraora, and Alolan Raichu, in turn also forming a pivoting core with Corviknight. Offensive Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Aerodactyl, and Tornadus-T appreciate Corviknight's slow pivoting to safely be brought onto the field; in return, they act as offensive checks to foes that Corviknight can't threaten by itself such as Great Tusk, Mega Gallade, and Ogerpon-W.
